attribution: The authors' own results as stated in the arXiv abstract. Not reproduced, re-run or re-claimed here. Quote wording is the authors'.

claims.quote: An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan.
We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants

claims.what: human vs uncalibrated simulated user, correcting fact omitted after an incorrect plan
claims.quote: human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%)

claims.what: initial-plan infeasibility, missing info vs all facts upfront
claims.quote: their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront

claims.what: uncovery rate, plan-changing vs plan-unchanged facts
claims.quote: Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often than facts that leave it unchanged (39-52% versus 32-41%).
This is ongoing work and will be updated.
